concept.name: Coppock curve
concept.definition: Edwin Coppock's long-term momentum indicator (Barron's, October 1965): a 10-period weighted moving average of the sum of the 14-period and 11-period rates of change, designed to flag major stock-market bottoms on monthly charts when it turns up from below zero.
concept.intuition: Coppock reportedly chose 11-14 months after hearing that grief over a loss typically runs about that long; the indicator waits out the mourning period and signals when the market has 'recovered.'
concept.mechanics: Coppock = WMA(ROC(14) + ROC(11), 10). Classic usage is monthly charts of major indexes, where a cross from negative to positive is the buy signal; platforms also allow shorter timeframes and adjusted parameters (e.g., 20,10,10 on daily charts).
concept.formula: Coppock = WMA(10) of [ROC(14) + ROC(11)], ROC(n) = ((C_t - C_{t-n}) / C_{t-n}) x 100.
concept.failure_modes: On monthly data it signals only every few years and can lag bottoms by months; designed for major equity indexes, on individual stocks or short timeframes it is just another smoothed ROC.
concept.misconceptions: Coppock never proposed sell signals - the positive-to-negative 'sell' cross is a later addition - and the 11/14/10 parameters were not statistically optimized.
concept.example: After a decline, if the 14-month and 11-month ROCs sum to +3 and rise, the 10-month WMA climbs toward +3, crossing zero for the classic buy signal.
